thread:
maria: Hey team — customer ACME (acct: acme-inc) says embeddings suddenly dropped from 1536 -> 768 after yesterday's deploy. They pinned open-embed-large:v2. Example response attached: {"vector_size": 768, "embedding": [...768 floats...]}. Can we triage?

devon: Thanks, can you paste the exact model string they sent and whether this is hosted/dedicated? Also, any request IDs or traces?

maria: Hosted API. Model header in customer calls: "model: open-embed-large:v2". No trace id from customer but they shared two curl calls that produced different lengths.

sanjay: tagging in routing logs. Quick note: we saw a spike in quantized pool utilization in us-west2 around the same time. There's an auto-fallback rule that can route to a quantized variant when capacity is low — quantized variant (open-embed-large-q:v1) emits 768-dim vectors. Could be that. :eyes:

maria: But they said they pinned the model. I thought pin prevented variant substitution?

devon: Pinning at the customer level pins the model NAME (open-embed-large:v2) but our runtime can still route to a binary-compatible variant if the variant is marked as a compatible fallback for that model. That compatibility map is in the model-routing service. We recently added a quantized fallback mapping to reduce cost/latency during load.

elaine: I reproduced locally with two successive calls. First call (single) returns 1536, second (batched) returns 768. Repro steps: ```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Model: open-embed-large:v2" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings | jq '.vector_size'
# => 1536

# Batched call
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Model: open-embed-large:v2" -d '{"input":["a","b"]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings | jq '.[0].vector_size'
# => 768
```

sanjay: That's useful — points to batching interaction. I think the pooling/batcher code will sometimes coalesce requests into the quantized pool for throughput. There's an edge where metadata (vector_size) gets taken from the variant chosen by the batch leader and applied to every item after batching — bug.

devon: Can you fetch a sample trace for a batched request? Look for headers: x-route-variant and x-fallback-used. If we see x-fallback-used: open-embed-large-q:v1 then it confirms fallback. Also check the routing service mapping for that customer id — was there an explicit variant pin?

eng-bot: deploy-notify: canary deploy 2026-03-16T21:41 applied to routing-service (sha: 4f8c9d).

sanjay: Found a trace: x-fallback-used=open-embed-large-q:v1 on a batched request. Also found a race where batch leader selection didn't preserve the customer's pin when the leader was matched from a different customer pool. That explains why some requests (single) are fine and some (batched) flip dims.

devon: Action items: 1) set P1 and notify oncall, 2) hotfix to preserve pin metadata across batching boundary (disable batch leader metadata override), 3) add a short-term routing rule to honor customer pin strictly (no fallback) for acme-inc, 4) backfill a monitor for vector_size variance per customer.

maria: I've told the customer the workaround: add header "x-force-variant: open-embed-large:v2" or temporarily pin to the explicit variant id. They've accepted the temporary workaround.

elaine: Additional note — billing/usage unaffected because tokens still counted, but embeddings post-processing in customer's pipeline failed. Customer provided sample vectors; we're coordinating a reingest if needed.

devon: I'll open an internal issue with repro steps and link the trace IDs. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.

maria: Thanks — please update this thread when patch is out.

eng-bot: incident-created: INC-2026-0041 (P1)

maria: ACK, thanks everyone.
